2609.00572.title: A Mathematical Framework for Legacy, Governance, and Decision Integrity in Enterprise AI
2609.00572.paper_summary: Enterprise artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in decisions that must remain lawful, explainable, adaptable, and accountable despite personnel turnover, model replacement, regulatory change, and shifting organizational incentives. Existing governance frameworks provide important principles but do not by themselves supply a compact mathematical language for evaluating whether an institution can preserve sound judgment over time. This paper develops a design-science framework for institutional legacy: the durable capacity of a decision system to continue producing beneficial, lawful, explainable, and adaptable outcomes after its original designers have stepped away. The framework contributes: (i) a normalized Legacy Score based on a penalized geometric mean of knowledge retention, governance, human oversight, adaptability, feedback learning, and jurisdictional fidelity; (ii) Decision Confidence and Decision Risk models separating evidentiary confidence from consequence; (iii) authority-aware retrieval and calibrated abstention; (iv) Decision Memory for governed organizational learning; (v) Regulatory Change Velocity mapping change exposure to review intervals; and (vi) a federated regulatory knowledge-graph architecture preserving provenance and legal hierarchy. The paper also proposes eight AI Decision Integrity Rules, an evaluation protocol, and a reproducible computational demonstration. The demonstration combines a deterministic stress test with 200 Monte Carlo replications of 10,000 synthetic decisions each, illustrating Legacy Score non-compensation and comparing consequence- and authority-aware routing with a matched-coverage confidence-only baseline. The contribution remains conceptual rather than field-validated; the simulation tests internal behavior, not production performance, and all parameters require context-specific calibration.
2609.00572.paper_summary_zh: 企業人工智慧越來越多地嵌入必須保持合法、可解釋、可適應和負責的決策中，儘管人員流動、模型更換、監管變化和組織激勵的轉變。現有的治理框架提供了重要的原則，但僅靠這些原則無法提供一種緊湊的數學語言來評估一個機構是否能夠隨著時間的推移保持良好的判斷。本文開發了一個針對機構遺產的設計科學框架：決策系統在其原始設計者退出後繼續產生有益、合法、可解釋和可適應結果的持久能力。該框架的貢獻包括：(i) 基於知識保留、治理、人為監督、適應性、反饋學習和管轄權忠誠度的懲罰幾何平均數的標準化遺產分數；(ii) 將證據信心與後果分開的決策信心和決策風險模型；(iii) 具權威意識的檢索和經過校準的棄權；(iv) 用於治理組織學習的決策記憶；(v) 將變更暴露映射到審查間隔的監管變更速度；以及(vi) 保留來源和法律層級的聯邦監管知識圖譜架構。本文還提出了八條人工智慧決策完整性規則、一個評估協議和一個可重複的計算演示。該演示結合了一個確定性壓力測試和200次蒙特卡羅重複，每次包含10,000個合成決策，說明了遺產分數的非補償性並比較了後果和權威意識路由與匹配覆蓋的僅信心基準。這一貢獻仍然是概念性的，而非經過現場驗證；模擬測試內部行為，而非生產性能，所有參數都需要特定上下文的校準。
2609.00572.author: Shorab Sarker et.al.
